skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Guides users through creating, naming, placing, and version-controlling Claude Code skills with correct YAML frontmatter and scope.
skill.summary: Create Claude Code skills with correct folders, frontmatter, naming, and Git workflow.
skill.author: ChinchillaEnterprises

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, and the hardcoded URL is only a repository reference. The filesystem findings are confirmed because the skill intentionally guides users toward persistent writes under ~/.claude/skills, which can affect assistant behavior globally. Additional contextual risk comes from the repeated instruction to commit and push global skills to a shared repository.

remediation.issue: Default global installation under hidden assistant directories
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating or editing files under ~/.claude/skills, and explain the cross-project persistence impact.

remediation.issue: Repeated Git push workflow for global skills
remediation.suggestion: Add a review step that checks for private project details, credentials, and sensitive instructions before any commit or push.

remediation.issue: Personal repository assumptions in public guidance
remediation.suggestion: Replace ChillSkills-specific instructions with configurable repository guidance, or clearly label that workflow as optional.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Global Assistant Skill Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents ~/.claude/skills as the default location and says most skills belong there. Following this guidance can install persistent assistant instructions that apply across all projects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple explicit lines identify ~/.claude/skills as the default global location and success criterion. The security impact is contextual persistence, not merely the presence of a hidden path.

semantic_findings.title: Shared Repository Publication Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly tells users to commit and push global skills to a shared ChillSkills repository. That workflow can publish private project details or sensitive instructions if a generated skill is not reviewed first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commit and push workflow is repeated in several sections and the repository is explicitly identified. The risk depends on user content, so confidence is high for the workflow and moderate for actual exposure.

content.value_statement: Creating AI skills can be confusing when folder scope, file names, and frontmatter rules are unclear. This skill gives a practical workflow for building Claude Code skills with consistent structure and version control.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to create global skills versus project-local skills.
Shows the expected folder layout for Claude Code skill files.
Lists required YAML frontmatter fields for skill discovery.
Provides naming rules for lowercase hyphenated skill names.
Outlines a Git workflow for committing and pushing global skills.
Includes checklists for creating, updating, and testing skills.
limitations: Assumes Claude Code skill conventions and may not match every assistant platform.
Uses a personal global skills repository workflow that may not fit all teams.
Does not validate the security or quality of generated skill instructions.
Requires care before writing to hidden assistant configuration folders.

use_cases.title: Create a Personal Skill Library
use_cases.description: Build reusable assistant skills with consistent names, folders, and frontmatter.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skill Creation
use_cases.description: Give contributors a repeatable checklist for adding skills to a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Teach Skill File Requirements
use_cases.description: Explain the structure needed for skill discovery, activation, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new reusable skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill creator guidance to help me create a global skill named [skill-name] for [purpose]. Include the required sections.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Skill Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Decide between global and project-local placement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill creator guidance to decide whether my skill for [workflow] should be global or project-local. Explain the placement choice.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Skill Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an existing draft before installation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill creator checklist to review my draft skill for naming, frontmatter, folder placement, and missing sections.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Shared Skill Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for teams managing multiple skills.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill creator guidance to design a team process for creating, reviewing, testing, and versioning shared Claude Code skills.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable skill for code review.
output: Recommended scope: global, because code review can apply across repositories.
Required sections: purpose, activation, workflow overview, critical rules, success criteria, and example.
Next step: create the skill file in the global skills folder after user approval.

output_examples.input: Review my skill draft before I install it.
output: The name follows the lowercase hyphen rule.
The frontmatter includes the required name and description fields.
The description should add clearer trigger words for activation.
The workflow should include a short testing step before committing.

output_examples.input: Should this project deployment skill be global?
output: Project-local is likely better if the workflow depends on one repository.
Global is better only if the same process applies across many repositories.
Document the reason for the chosen scope before installing the skill.

best_practices: Confirm scope before writing files to global or project-local assistant folders.
Use clear trigger words in each skill description so activation is predictable.
Test a new skill before committing it to a shared repository.
anti_patterns: Do not place project-specific instructions in a global skill by default.
Do not omit YAML frontmatter from the skill file.
Do not push private or unreviewed skill content to a shared repository.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code skills with the expected file structure, naming, frontmatter, and workflow sections.

faq.question: Does it create skills automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance. File creation and Git actions should still require user review and approval.

faq.question: When should a skill be global?
faq.answer: A skill should be global when it is reusable across repositories and does not depend on one project.

faq.question: When should a skill be project-local?
faq.answer: A skill should be project-local when it only makes sense for one repository or one project workflow.

faq.question: Why is YAML frontmatter important?
faq.answer: The frontmatter provides the name and description that allow the assistant to discover and activate the skill.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing a skill?
faq.answer: Review the scope, trigger words, safety constraints, file path, and any content that might expose private information.
